# GroupScopedToken — a bearer that looks like `request.user` but is capped at one group

- **Kind**: feature
- **Date**: 2026-07-30 (re-scoped 2026-07-31)
- **Requested by**: Ian
- **Source**: design discussion while scoping #943; unblocks API access for gated-site visitors without handing out platform JWTs
- **Status**: v2 plan, red-teamed and build-ready. The v1 blockers (O2/O3/O10) are resolved by **splitting the item**: this item ships the credential + confinement with a **service-level mint only**; browser delivery / mint selection moved to a follow-up item. The v2 draft was itself independently red-teamed (6 objections, 2 blocking — Group LIST bypass, unguarded chat endpoints); all verified and amended into the plan below.

Apply rules: django-mojo-build-conventions

## Problem

A hosted site's visitor needs to call the API as themselves — read protected content,
submit forms, search. Today the only bearer that does that is a full platform JWT, which
grants everything that account can reach across every workspace it belongs to.

Handing that to JavaScript on a page whose content a tenant controls means the tenant
receives a platform credential for every visitor who signs in. Maestro #908 (done)
deliberately routes a scoped ticket to tenant hosts and keeps the JWT off them entirely
(its design decision 4); #943 (done) made the handoff mint destination-aware. What is
still missing is the *credential* those flows could hand to a tenant origin: a bearer
that authenticates as the visitor but is confined to one group.

A JWT is not inert either: `mojo/apps/account/models/member.py:125` returns True
unconditionally for `all` / `authenticated` / `member`, so any signed-in identity passes
every endpoint whose perms are one of those.

## What to build (this item — "part 1")

A third bearer scheme alongside `bearer` (JWT) and `apikey`:

    Authorization: grouptoken <token>

It authenticates as a real user, but authorization resolves **only** through that user's
membership in one named group. No other group, no workspace, no cross-tenant reach.

**Minting is service-level only in this item**: `group_token.mint(user, group)` for
in-process callers (e.g. a #908-style gate leg on the platform, or a deployment's own
trusted code). No REST endpoint mints one; no login/handoff behavior changes. The
browser-delivery half (hosted auth pages minting one instead of a JWT, mojo-auth.js
storage rules) is the split-off item.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `Authorization: grouptoken <t>` authenticates as the signed user with authorization
      resolved only through their membership in the signed group
- [ ] No new DB table or row per token — signed stateless payload
- [ ] `group_token.mint(user, group)` refuses: superusers, inactive users, inactive
      groups/ancestors, non-direct membership
- [ ] Epoch bump (`revoke_group_tokens` action, service accessor) revokes every
      outstanding token for that group; rotating the user's `auth_key` revokes that
      user's tokens
- [ ] Bad signature / expired / epoch mismatch / inactive user / inactive group or
      ancestor / removed membership → 401, no partial identity, no 500s on malformed input
- [ ] A group token cannot reach another group's data — including via `?group=`,
      `account=group-<id>` metrics params, every room-resolving chat endpoint, docit
      search, assistant context, `group/<pk>/member`, and Group records (detail AND
      list)
- [ ] A group token cannot be exchanged or upgraded into a full JWT (not via `bearer`
      replay, `refresh_token`, `auth/handoff`, or any credential-mutation endpoint)
- [ ] `denies_key_backed_session` endpoints refuse it; `requires_global_perms` refuses it
      even with `allow_api_keys=True`
- [ ] `GET /api/user/me` works (read-only self-bootstrap); every User write is refused
- [ ] Registered through `AUTH_BEARER_HANDLERS` settings (opt-in per deployment; no
      default-on parsing surface)
- [ ] Tests per the testing plan below
- [ ] Docs: both tracks + settings reference + CHANGELOG

## Out of scope

- **Mint selection / browser delivery** — hosted auth pages, handoff/exchange
  integration, mojo-auth.js — split to the follow-up item (see "Split" below)
- Per-path or per-endpoint scoping inside a group — group membership is the boundary
- Any consumer-hosted login/register UI
- Migrating existing `ApiKey` usage
- WebSocket/realtime auth for group tokens (explicitly refused in v1; follow-up if wanted)

---

## Plan (v2)

### D1 — Token format and signing (no JWT, deliberately)

Format: `gt1.<b64payload>.<sig>`
- `b64payload` = `crypto.b64_encode({"u": user_id, "g": group_id, "e": epoch, "iat": unix_ts})`
- `sig` = `crypto.sign("gt1." + b64payload, user.get_auth_key())` — HMAC-SHA256 hex via
  `mojo.helpers.crypto` (`sign`/`verify` = `generate_signature`/`verify_signature` in
  `mojo/helpers/crypto/sign.py`; `verify` uses `hmac.compare_digest`, constant time).
  The version prefix is **inside** the HMAC'd string — this is the O14 fix: it
  domain-separates the gt1 family from `utils/tokens.py:_generate` (`tokens.py:81-82`),
  which signs a bare b64 payload with the same key. Full 64-char hex signature, **not**
  the 6-char truncation `tokens.py:86` uses (that truncation is safe only because those
  tokens carry a server-stored single-use `jti`, which a session bearer has no
  equivalent of).
- Secret source: `user.get_auth_key()` (`mojo/models/auth.py:34`, stored in
  `mojo_secrets`). Two free properties: rotating `auth_key` (what
  `POST /api/auth/sessions/revoke` already does) also kills that user's group tokens,
  and a token forged against user A's key cannot be replayed as user B.
- The SECRET_KEY_FALLBACKS work (`c72524cc`) does not apply here — `crypto.verify` with
  an explicit per-user key does no fallback iteration (verified in
  `mojo/helpers/crypto/sign.py:42-54`).

**Why not reuse `JWToken`.** A JWT signed with `user.get_auth_key()` would be accepted
verbatim by `User.validate_jwt` under `Authorization: bearer`, and by `on_refresh_token`
(`rest/user.py:125-140`) as a `refresh_token` — trading the scoped token for a full
unscoped JWT pair. The `gt1.` format cannot be parsed by `jwt.decode` at all, so the
"cannot be upgraded into a JWT" AC holds *by construction* (v1 red team verified:
`jwt.decode` raises `DecodeError`; both replay paths 401).

### D2 — TTL

`GROUP_TOKEN_TTL`, default `3600` (matches `MAGIC_LOGIN_TOKEN_TTL` /
`PASSWORD_RESET_TOKEN_TTL`). No refresh path — expiry means re-mint. Clock skew
tolerance is a module constant `_MAX_FUTURE_SKEW = 60`; not a setting, per KISS.

### D3 — Epoch storage: `group.metadata["protected"]["group_token_epoch"]`

No migration. The `protected` root key is REST-guarded by
`MojoModel._can_edit_protected_json` — superuser or `RestMeta.PROTECTED_JSON_PERMS`,
which on `Group` is `["admin_compliance", "admin_verify"]` (`group.py:51`), so a tenant
group admin with `manage_group` cannot write it via REST and cannot rewind the epoch to
un-revoke tokens. Accessors `get_protected_metadata` / `set_protected_metadata` exist
(`group.py:268/:273`). Absent key reads as `0`; a payload missing `e` fails closed.
Read-modify-write is not atomic — two simultaneous bumps can land `N+1` instead of
`N+2`; both intend "invalidate everything issued before now" and the window self-heals
within TTL. Documented, accepted. v1 red team verified: `Group.metadata` is uncached
(epoch bumps are immediately visible cross-process), and `_can_edit_protected_json`
really does exclude tenant admins.

New on `Group`: `get_group_token_epoch()` / `bump_group_token_epoch()` (increment-only),
plus POST_SAVE_ACTIONS entry `revoke_group_tokens` → `on_action_revoke_group_tokens`
(discrete key per the board's action conventions; gated by `Group.SAVE_PERMS` through
`check_edit_permission`, so a group-token session can never trigger it — the swap in D5
makes that hook deny restricted identities).

### D4 — Mint surface: service-level only (REPLACES v1's mint selection — the v2 decision)

`mint(user, group, issued_at=None)` in `mojo/apps/account/services/group_token.py`.
Guards, mirroring `ApiKey.validate_acting_user` (`api_key.py:295-317`): never a
superuser; user active; group effectively active; **direct** active `GroupMember`
(`check_parents=False` — delegation must not exceed the delegator). Raises
`PermissionDeniedException` on refusal.

**No REST mint endpoint, no login change, no handoff change.** This dissolves v1's three
blocking objections rather than answering them:

- O3 (login's `group_uuid` is attacker-omittable) — nothing about `/api/login` selects
  tokens anymore; login mints JWTs exactly as today.
- O2 (registration pin misses OAuth/invite) — there is no pin.
- O10 (pin bricks offboarded accounts) — there is no pin.

The security claim this item makes is correspondingly narrower and *enforceable*: **a
group token, wherever one exists, cannot escape its group.** The claim "a gated-site
visitor's browser never receives a full JWT" belongs to the delivery flow — the split
item — and per #908's shipped design that flow runs server-side on platform origins
(`gate/return` consumes the handoff code in-process), where it can call `mint()`
directly. The in-process consumer needs nothing further from this repo to stop shipping
JWTs to tenant pages.

Tests mint in the test process via the service (testit shares Postgres with the test
server; the token is stateless, so a test-side mint validates server-side — same for
epoch bumps, which are uncached).

### D5 — How the bearer presents itself to the guards

The handler sets `request.group_token = <GroupScopedToken instance>`. New predicate in
`mojo/helpers/request.py`:

```
def restricted_identity(request):
    # The machine/confined identity for this request, if any: an ApiKey or a
    # GroupScopedToken. Both are bearer credentials whose authority must stay
    # inside one group tree regardless of whose identity they carry.
    return getattr(request, "api_key", None) or getattr(request, "group_token", None)
```

`is_key_backed_session()` (`request.py:42-54`) becomes
`restricted_identity(request) is not None`; `is_override_user_session()` (`:57-68`)
becomes `ident is not None and bool(getattr(ident, "override_user", False))`. Docstrings
updated to name both credential kinds.

That one swap covers, with no call-site edits (verified by full grep):
- `@md.denies_key_backed_session()` — all 22 decorated endpoints (`decorators/auth.py:103`),
  **including `POST /api/auth/handoff` (`rest/user.py:220`)** — which is what makes
  "cannot be upgraded via handoff→exchange" hold. (#943's build note: the regression
  test for this must send a valid `redirect_uri`, or it 400s for the wrong reason.)
- `_deny_machine_identity_without_active_group` (`decorators/auth.py:55`) — group tokens
  carry an active group context, so `requires_perms`/`requires_group_perms` resolve
  member grants in the token group with `check_user=False` (`:151/:170/:213/:231` key on
  `is_override_user_session`, and the token's `override_user=True` makes the global-dict
  short-circuit skip).
- The owner chokes — detail (`models/rest.py:460`) and LIST twin (`:779-781`). A group
  token never satisfies `owner` perms: owner-scoped groupless models are the credential
  family (Passkey, UserAPIKey, UserTOTP, OAuthConnection, RegisteredDevice), and
  visitor-owned content on a gated site is group-scoped, which resolves through the
  group branch instead.
- The group branch gate (`models/rest.py:491`) and `check_user=False` (`:547`).
- `mojo/apps/dnsman/rest/gates.py:42` and `ApiKey._can_manage_acting_user`
  (`api_key.py:261`) — both deny group tokens too; fail-closed, correct.

`GroupScopedToken` duck-types only the surface those guards touch — **not** a model,
never saved:

| member | value / behaviour |
|---|---|
| `group` / `group_id` | the signed Group |
| `user` | the signed User |
| `override_user` | `True` |
| `pk` | `None` |
| `is_active` | `True` |
| `limits` | `{}` |
| `is_group_allowed(g)` | `g is not None and g.pk == self.group_id and g.is_effectively_active()` — strict equality, **no descendants** |
| `has_permission(perms)` | always `False` — the token itself never satisfies a grant; combined with the D9/D10 gates, no authority resolves outside the signed group |
| `get_groups(...)` | `Group.objects.filter(pk=self.group_id)` when effectively active, else `none()` |
| `get_groups_with_permission(perms)` | the same single-group queryset iff `group.user_has_permission(user, perms, check_user=False)`, else `none()` — mirrors the detail path exactly |

### D6 — Registration: settings-driven, opt-in per deployment

`AUTH_BEARER_HANDLERS` gains
`{"grouptoken": "mojo.apps.account.services.group_token.validate_token"}` and
`AUTH_BEARER_NAME_MAP` gains a `"grouptoken": "user"` entry — **in settings, not in the
hardcoded `AUTH_BEARER_HANDLERS_CACHE`** (`middleware/auth.py:14-19`). A deployment that
doesn't register the scheme rejects `Authorization: grouptoken …` with 401 "Invalid
token type" exactly as today — no new default-on parsing surface, no flag day (the #943
lesson). Without the NAME_MAP entry the middleware would `setattr(request, "grouptoken",
user)` and `request.user` would never populate — both entries are required.
**Both settings replace their defaults wholesale — there is no merge**
(`settings.get_static` with a default dict, `middleware/auth.py:12,:19`). The docs and
settings reference MUST show the complete three-entry NAME_MAP
(`{"bearer": "user", "apikey": "user", "grouptoken": "user"}`): a deployment that
declares only the grouptoken entry silently breaks JWT and apikey auth —
`request.user` never populates and every request degrades to anonymous 403s with no
diagnostic (v2 challenge C4).
`bin/create_testproject` writes both maps wholesale (`create_testproject:233-237`), so
the generated settings gain both entries; the builder must re-run it before the suite
(settings regen only, no migration).

### D7 — WebSocket: refused

`mojo/apps/realtime/auth.py` calls handlers with `request=None`; the handler's first
check returns `(None, "Invalid token")` when `request is None` — explicit fail-closed
early return (the ApiKey handler documents the same situation at `api_key.py:632-637`).
v1 red team verified the realtime path wraps handlers and refuses cleanly.

### D8 — `/api/user/me`: read-only self (resolves v1 O12)

`User.check_edit_permission` (`models/user.py:992-1005`) is the choke point for
`/api/user/<pk>` — consulted for VIEW-by-pk too, since User defines no
`check_view_permission`. New branch ahead of the api_key branch:

```
group_token = getattr(request, "group_token", None)
if group_token is not None:
    return (request.method == "GET" and "owner" in perms
            and self.is_request_user(request))
```

(Pass `request` into `is_request_user` explicitly rather than relying on the
`active_request` context var — v2 challenge nit. Method-sniffing here is sound:
`on_rest_request` dispatches strictly on `request.method`, every write-key evaluation
arrives with a write verb, User has no `CAN_BATCH`, and `POST_SAVE_ACTIONS` only run
inside the save path. The FK-attach VIEW check runs with the outer request's method
(POST on a save) and therefore denies — a tightening. Known cosmetic edge: a `HEAD`
to `/api/user/me` 403s; accepted.)

- `GET /api/user/me` (`rest/user.py:26-32` routes to `on_rest_request(request,
  request.user.pk)`) → 200. The documented client bootstrap ("call /me; on failure
  refresh") keeps working. The `default` graph exposes no group memberships (verified
  `user.py:141-234`), so nothing cross-tenant leaks; the visitor's own contact fields
  are within a credential that authenticates *as them*.
- Any write (`POST /api/user/me`, password/email change, `revoke_sessions` and every
  other POST_SAVE_ACTION, DELETE) → 403: tenant-page JS must never mutate the platform
  account. Credential endpoints (totp/passkeys/email-change/api-keys) are additionally
  covered by `denies_key_backed_session`.
- Reading another user by pk → False (self check fails) → 403, as for ApiKeys.

### D9 — `requires_global_perms`: group tokens never pass (resolves v1 O5)

`decorators/auth.py:284` denies key-backed sessions unless `allow_api_keys=True`. That
flag means "a provisioned ApiKey is the intended caller" (one in-framework use: the
federation ingest `system/geoip/sync`, `rest/device.py:87`); a visitor-grade group
token is not that, and the check after it reads the **real user's global dict**, which a
group token must never reach. Add, before the allow_api_keys check:

```
if getattr(request, "group_token", None) is not None:
    raise mojo.errors.PermissionDeniedException()
```

plus a docstring line. `allow_api_keys` keeps meaning exactly "ApiKey".

### D10 — Confinement at gates that bypass model security (resolves v1 O1, O9, O11)

New helper in `mojo/helpers/request.py`:

```
def identity_allows_group(request, group):
    # Fail-closed tenant check for endpoints that authorize against an
    # arbitrary caller-named group (metrics account=group-<id>, chat room
    # helpers, ...) rather than through model security's instance re-bind.
    ident = restricted_identity(request)
    if ident is None:
        return True
    return group is not None and ident.is_group_allowed(group)
```

Applied at every direct gate the v1 red team enumerated (all verified against the
current tree):

1. **`Group.check_view_permission` / `check_edit_permission`** (`group.py:611-613`,
   `:636-638`) — v1's blocking O1. Swap `getattr(request, "api_key", None)` for
   `restricted_identity(request)`. For a group token: `is_group_allowed` is true only
   for its own group and `has_permission` is always False → **all Group-record CRUD
   denies, own group included** (fail-closed; tenant UI reads branding from
   `public_auth_config`, not the Group record). ApiKey behavior is bit-identical. These
   hooks are the only gate for Group detail ops — `_evaluate_permission` returns from
   them before the instance re-bind (`rest.py:420-438`), which is why O1 was a full
   cross-tenant read/write for any-group members and global-perm holders.
   **Plus the LIST verb** (v2 challenge C1): `Group.on_rest_handle_list`
   (`group.py:841-876`) is a model-level override whose fallback derives identity from
   `request.api_key` (`:859-861`) and otherwise reads `request.user.get_groups(...)` —
   every group the visitor belongs to, cross-tenant. Group tokens get an explicit
   early branch there: return `cls.on_rest_list(request, cls.objects.none())` (empty
   list, matching the no-groups arm at `:874-876`) — Group records are fully opaque to
   group tokens, list and detail consistent. The ApiKey leg (`:859-873`) is untouched.
2. **`GET /api/account/group/<pk>/member`** (`rest/group.py:102-122`) — v1's O9. After
   `request.group = Group.get_active(pk)`, add
   `if not identity_allows_group(request, request.group): raise` (same single
   PermissionDenied raise site, preserving the no-oracle contract).
3. **Metrics helpers** (`apps/metrics/rest/helpers.py`) — v1's O11 lead case. Two
   distinct rules (v2 challenge C3 refined this — they must not be conflated):
   - `identity_allows_group(request, group)` — required **unconditionally for every
     restricted identity** in `_check_group_account_permission` (`:8-23`), after
     resolving the group and before either grant path. This is the tenant bound.
   - The `request.user.has_permission` global short-circuits (`:13`, `:32`, and the
     `global`/custom-perms branches `:51-53/:59-64/:78-80/:86-103`) are skipped only
     when `is_override_user_session(request)` — i.e. exactly the sessions where
     `request.user` is a real User whose untenanted global dict would be consulted
     (override ApiKeys, and group tokens via the predicate swap). For a
     reference-mode/unlinked ApiKey, `request.user` IS the ApiKey and that read is the
     key's own group-bounded dict (`helpers/request.py:57-68` documents exactly this) —
     skipping it there would break working deployments.
   `_check_user_account_permission`'s self-check (`:35`) stays — own metrics are the
   acting user's own data. **The `identity_allows_group` bound also closes the same
   pre-existing cross-tenant read for override ApiKeys** — a documented behavior fix,
   not a regression: it aligns metrics with `is_group_allowed`, the contract every
   other gate enforces. CHANGELOG entry required.
4. **Chat — every room-resolving endpoint**, not just the admin helpers (v2 challenge
   C2; the v1 red team under-scoped this). `room/join` (`apps/chat/rest/rooms.py:26-73`)
   authorizes via `room.group.user_has_permission(request.user, ["chat","manage_chat"])`
   with `check_user=True` and no identity consultation — a group token for A joins a
   room in B (a cross-tenant **write**: membership row, system message, realtime
   publish). `room/members` (`:246-262`) and `room/messages`
   (`apps/chat/rest/messages.py`) serve rosters/bodies through the groupless
   `ChatMembership`/message models, and `room/online` (`:265-290`) has no gate beyond
   auth. Fix: every endpoint in `chat/rest/{rooms,messages}.py` that resolves a room
   from request params gains `if not identity_allows_group(request, room.group):
   raise` immediately after resolving the room — a `room.group` of None (personal/DM
   rooms) denies restricted identities, fail-closed. The `user_has_permission` calls in
   those endpoints and in `_check_room_admin`/`_check_room_moderator` (`:293-314`) get
   the `check_user = not is_override_user_session(request)` discipline; the bare
   `request.user.has_permission` fallbacks (`:300/:312`) are skipped under the same
   predicate.
5. **Assistant** (`apps/assistant/rest/assistant.py:70-80`) — the VIEW_PERMS loop reads
   only the global dict and then `build_context` reads arbitrary model rows. Deny
   restricted identities outright at the top of the endpoint.
6. **Docit search** (`apps/docit/services/search.py:25-46`) — `visible_groups` is
   already identity-aware via its `api_key` parameter; change the REST call site(s)
   (`apps/docit/rest/search.py`) to pass `restricted_identity(request)` (duck-typed:
   `get_groups_with_permission` is on the surface). The
   `user.has_permission(GLOBAL_READ_PERMS)` unrestricted branch is then unreachable
   for group tokens.
7. **The remaining in-framework global-dict short-circuits on group-confined writes**
   (v2 challenge C5): `on_group_invite_member` (`rest/group.py:36-63`) — its
   `request.group.user_has_permission(request.user, perms)` call (`:54`) gains the
   `check_user = not is_override_user_session(request)` discipline, so a group token
   (or override key) can invite only with member-level manage grants in the token
   group; `GroupMember.can_change_permission` (`member.py:84-93`) and
   `ApiKey.can_change_permission` (`api_key.py:191-219`) — their
   `request.user.has_permission(["manage_groups","manage_users"])` short-circuits
   (`member.py:85`, `api_key.py:204`) are skipped under the same predicate, so
   permission assignment falls through to the requester's real member row. Reference-
   mode ApiKeys are unaffected (their `request.user` reads are the key's own dict).

`ChatRoom.CREATE_PERMS = ["authenticated"]` (short-circuit at `rest.py:362-363`) stays:
creation binds to `request.group` (the token's group — the dispatcher guard blocks
rebinds), so a visitor creating chat rooms in their own gated group is in-contract.

**Known gap, documented, not built**: `is_key_backed_session` consumers and
`identity_allows_group` cover the framework's own gates. Third-party apps that read
`request.user.has_permission` directly remain the deployment's responsibility — the
django_developer docs get an explicit "writing group-token-safe endpoints" section
(use `requires_perms`/model security, or call the two helpers).

### The `_evaluate_permission` / dispatcher / LIST sites (mechanics)

- `models/rest.py:395` — the pre-hook inactive-instance-group gate keys on
  `getattr(request, "api_key", None)`; use `restricted_identity(request)`.
- `models/rest.py:503` — `request.api_key.is_group_allowed(...)` inside the (swapped)
  key-backed group branch → `restricted_identity(request).is_group_allowed(...)`.
- `models/rest.py:555-588` — the groupless/null-group `elif hasattr(request, 'api_key')
  and request.api_key:` branch must become `elif restricted_identity(request):`, with a
  **group-token deny before the `ALLOW_API_KEY_GLOBAL` read**: that flag is an
  ApiKey-specific opt-in and a visitor token must not inherit it
  (`branch="group_token.groupless_denied"`). Without this restructure a group token
  falls past the elif to the flat `request.user.has_permission` at `:595` — the v1 plan
  underspecified this; it is load-bearing for every groupless model.
- `models/rest.py:805-809` — LIST identity: `identity = restricted_identity(request) or
  request.user`.
- `decorators/http.py:104-106` and `:140-142` — dispatcher `?group=`/`group_uuid=`
  rebind guards: `ident = restricted_identity(request); if ident and request.group and
  not ident.is_group_allowed(request.group): 403`. Keep the truthiness structure
  exactly (v1 O13: substituting the guard along with the call 500s every `?group=`
  request from a normal JWT user). Load-bearing: without it a token could rebind
  `request.group` to any other group the member belongs to. A bogus `?group=` that
  resolves None clears `request.group` and then every group-scoped path fails closed
  via the groupless deny — same as ApiKeys today.

### Validate order (`validate_token(token, request)`)

Entire body wrapped in try/except (v1 O4: `middleware/auth.py:51` calls the handler
bare; `b64_decode` raises `binascii.Error`/`UnicodeDecodeError`/`json.JSONDecodeError`,
and `hmac.compare_digest` raises `TypeError` on a non-ASCII signature segment, which a
latin-1-decoded `HTTP_AUTHORIZATION` can carry — `User.validate_jwt` guards exactly
this). Unexpected exception → `logit.exception` + generic failure. All failures return
the same `(None, "Invalid group token")` (no account/group-state oracle) except expiry:

1. `request is None` → fail (D7)
2. 3 dot-separated parts, `gt1` prefix
3. `b64_decode` → dict with int `u`, `g`, `e`, `iat`
4. `User.objects.filter(pk=u, is_active=True).first()` else fail
5. `crypto.verify("gt1." + parts[1], parts[2], user.get_auth_key())` (D1 domain tag)
6. `now - iat > GROUP_TOKEN_TTL` → `(None, "Group token expired")`; `iat - now > 60` → fail
7. `user.is_superuser` → `logit.error` + fail (mirror of `api_key.py:595-604`)
8. Group by pk, `is_effectively_active()` else fail (covers the inactive-ancestor AC)
9. epoch mismatch (`payload.e != group.get_group_token_epoch()`) → fail
10. direct active `GroupMember` (`check_parents=False`) else fail
11. success: set `request.group = group`, `request.group_token = <GroupScopedToken>`,
    `request.acting_user = user`; return `(user, None)` — middleware then sets
    `request.user` via NAME_MAP and `request.bearer = "grouptoken"`

### Testing plan — `tests/test_auth/group_token.py`

Baseline first per `.claude/rules/build-baseline.md` (`bin/run_tests --agent`, record in
the item; red baseline stops the build). Setup: tenant groups A and B (B sibling; plus a
child of A and an inactive-parent case), visitor member of both A and B, a group-scoped
model with member perms (pick an existing fixture model used by other permission tests),
staff user with global perms. Clean up before create per testing rules; every assert
carries a message.

1. Happy path: mint(visitor, A) → GET group-scoped rows in A → 200; `request.user`
   attribution works.
2. Cross-tenant reach: same token → B rows 403; `?group=B` 403 (dispatcher);
   `account=group-B` metrics fetch 403; `account=user-<other_pk>` metrics 403;
   `group/<B>/member` 403; A-child rows 403 (strict equality, no descendants).
3. Group record CRUD + LIST: GET/POST `/api/account/group/<A>` 403 (D10.1) — and for a
   token-user who also holds global `manage_groups`, still 403 (the O1 regression);
   `GET /api/account/group` returns an empty list even though the visitor belongs to
   A and B (the C1 regression).
4. Groupless models: staff user via group token → `/api/user` list empty/denied;
   `GET /api/user/<other_pk>` 403; a groupless-model VIEW with global perms 403
   (`group_token.groupless_denied`).
5. Revocation: epoch bump → 401; `auth_key` rotation → 401; membership removal → 401;
   group deactivated → 401; ancestor deactivated → 401; user deactivated → 401.
6. Expiry + skew: `issued_at` beyond TTL → 401 "Group token expired"; `iat` 120s in the
   future → 401.
7. Tampering: flipped payload byte, truncated/6-char sig, non-ASCII sig segment,
   garbage b64, 2/4 parts, JWT pasted under `grouptoken`, gt1 token under `bearer`,
   gt1 token as `refresh_token` → all clean 401s, never 500.
8. Upgrade paths: `POST /api/auth/handoff` with valid `redirect_uri` under a group
   token → 403 (per #943's note); `revoke_sessions` action + email-change request +
   TOTP list + UserAPIKey create → 403.
9. `requires_global_perms`: `system/geoip/sync` with a global-perm-holding token user →
   403 (D9).
10. `/api/user/me`: GET → 200 with own identity; POST (display_name) → 403.
11. Mint guards: superuser refused; non-member refused; member-of-parent-only refused
    (direct membership rule); inactive group refused.
12. Superuser hard block at validate: token minted (forced via internals) for a user
    later promoted to superuser → 401.
13. `validate_token(token, None)` → refused (D7, unit-level).
14. Chat cross-tenant (the C2 regression, endpoint-level): visitor has a `chat`-perm
    membership in B; under an A-token `POST room/join` on a B channel → 403 and no
    `ChatMembership` row is created; `GET room/members` and `GET room/messages` on a B
    room → 403; a room with `group=None` → 403 for the token session.
15. Docit search under an A-token returns only A-tenant results even when the visitor
    holds a member read grant in B (and a global-read staff visitor gets A-only, not
    unrestricted).
16. Assistant context endpoint under a group token → 403 (D10.5).
17. Invite confinement (C5): a global-`manage_groups` staff visitor under an A-token →
    `POST group/member/invite` for A → 403 (no member-level manage grant in A).
18. Opt-in registration (C6): with `th.server_settings` clearing the grouptoken
    entries, `Authorization: grouptoken <valid>` → 401 "Invalid token type"; restore
    and it authenticates.
19. Reference-mode ApiKey pin (C3): an unlinked key with `view_metrics` in its own
    dict still reads `account=group-<its own group>` metrics 200 (guards the
    short-circuit-skip predicate), while an override key acting as a two-tenant member
    reading `account=group-<other>` → 403 (the deliberate fix).

Regression watch: the metrics/chat/invite identity guards change override-ApiKey
behavior — run those modules' suites and fix fallout as part of this item.

### Documentation plan

- `docs/django_developer/account/auth.md` (+ README index): new "Group-scoped tokens"
  section — format, mint API, revocation (epoch + auth_key), confinement semantics,
  the known-gap paragraph and "writing group-token-safe endpoints" guidance (D10).
- `docs/django_developer/helpers/settings_reference.md`: `GROUP_TOKEN_TTL`,
  `AUTH_BEARER_HANDLERS`/`AUTH_BEARER_NAME_MAP` grouptoken entries (opt-in note).
- `docs/web_developer/account/authentication.md`: the `grouptoken` scheme from the
  consumer side — what it can/cannot call (`/me` read-only; no credential endpoints; no
  refresh), 401 semantics incl. the one distinct expiry message.
- `CHANGELOG.md`: feature entry + the metrics/chat override-ApiKey confinement fix.

### Split — follow-up item (filed at `scoped`, not `planned`)

"Hosted auth delivers a GroupScopedToken to gated destinations" — the browser-delivery
half, carrying v1's unresolved material: destination-keyed selection at the
handoff/exchange boundary (mint the code with a token-mode stamped server-side from the
#943 destination + `Group.resolve_by_auth_domain`; `auth/exchange` returns a group-token
package instead of `jwt_login` for such codes — selection at the delivery boundary,
where #943 made the destination trustworthy, never at login), plus the client work:
`token_type` in auth responses, `saveTokens` clear-on-absence (v1 O8), refresh-loop
suppression (v1 O7), `getTokenPayload`/`isTokenExpired` gt1 handling, and `jwt_login`'s
side-effect ordering if any server flow changes (v1 O6). O2/O10 (the per-user pin) stay
dead — no pin. Its open decision: the exact selection config (auth_config key vs
resolver hook) and whether `fire_user_login` fires on a token-mode exchange.

## Challenge

### v1 round (2026-07-30) — 14 objections, 3 blocking; all now dispositioned

| # | v1 finding | v2 disposition |
|---|---|---|
| O1 | Group's own hooks key on `request.api_key`; group token fell through to user branch → cross-tenant Group read/write. **Blocking.** | **amended** — D10.1 swaps both hooks to `restricted_identity`; regression test 3. |
| O2 | Registration pin missed OAuth/invite signup. **Blocking.** | **dissolved** — no pin exists (D4); the delivery item never re-introduces one. |
| O3 | Login `group_uuid` attacker-omittable; auth-domain fallback dead in split-host deployments. **Blocking.** | **dissolved** — login is untouched (D4); selection moves to the handoff destination boundary in the split item. |
| O4 | Handler called bare; malformed tokens → 500s. | **amended** — validate order wraps everything (try/except + generic fail). |
| O5 | `requires_global_perms(allow_api_keys=True)` would read the user's global dict. | **amended** — D9 hard-denies group tokens there. |
| O6 | `jwt_login` insertion point contradicted fire_user_login claim. | **moved** — no login change here; carried into the split item's open decisions. |
| O7 | `/api/refresh_token` + client auto-refresh overwrite the group token with a JWT. | **split** — server side is safe by construction (a gt1 token fails `validate_jwt`); the client-storage rules go with the delivery item. |
| O8 | mojo-auth.js misparses gt1 / stale scheme in localStorage. | **moved** — delivery item (no client change in this item). |
| O9 | `group/<pk>/member` cross-tenant read. | **amended** — D10.2 guard; regression test 2. |
| O10 | Pin was superuser-only to remove; offboarding bricked logins. | **dissolved** — no pin. |
| O11 | Direct `request.user.has_permission` gates in metrics/chat/assistant/docit leak cross-tenant. | **amended** — D10.3-6 fix all four (also fixes the pre-existing override-ApiKey metrics/chat leak); known-gap paragraph documents the boundary for third-party apps. |
| O12 | `/me` 403 broke the documented client bootstrap. | **amended** — D8: GET-self allowed, writes denied. |
| O13 | Dispatcher guard truthiness trap (500 on `?group=` for JWT users). | **amended** — explicitly encoded in the http.py step. |
| O14 | No domain separation vs `utils/tokens.py` signatures. | **amended** — D1 signs `"gt1." + payload`. |

v1 additionally verified (attacked and held): no JWT upgrade by construction; WebSocket
refusal; epoch not cache-stale; `_can_edit_protected_json` excludes tenant admins;
throttle identity resolves to the user; the happy path end-to-end; the
`denies_key_backed_session` surface via the predicate swap.

### v2 round (2026-07-31) — 6 objections; 2 blocking, all verified and amended

An independent fresh-context red team attacked the v2 draft. The orchestrator
re-verified every objection against the tree before dispositioning. None were rebutted.

- **C1 (blocking) — `Group.on_rest_handle_list` is a second, model-level LIST identity
  path the draft never touched.** `group.py:841-876` overrides the generic LIST; its
  fallback derives identity from `request.api_key` (`:859-861`) and otherwise reads
  `request.user.get_groups(...)` — so `GET /api/account/group` under an A-token listed
  every group the visitor belongs to, cross-tenant, defeating D10.1's "own group
  included" claim for the list verb. **amended** — explicit group-token empty-list
  branch in that override + regression test 3.
- **C2 (blocking) — the chat endpoints that matter never call the two patched
  helpers.** `room/join` (`rooms.py:26-73`, a cross-tenant WRITE: membership +
  system message + realtime publish), `room/members` (`:246-262`, roster via the
  groupless `ChatMembership`), `room/messages` (`messages.py`), `room/online`
  (`:265-290`) all authorize against a caller-named `room_id` with no identity
  consultation; only `room/member/add|remove|…` used `_check_room_admin`. **amended**
  — D10.4 rewritten: `identity_allows_group` after room resolution in every
  room-resolving endpoint in both files (None-group rooms deny restricted identities),
  plus `check_user` discipline; endpoint-level regression test 14.
- **C3 — skipping the metrics global short-circuits for ALL restricted identities
  breaks reference-mode/unlinked ApiKeys**, whose `request.user` IS the ApiKey and
  whose `has_permission` read is the key's own group-bounded dict
  (`helpers/request.py:57-68` documents the distinction; the fallthrough
  `group.user_has_permission(<ApiKey>, …)` then returns False at `group.py:213`).
  **amended** — the two-rule split in D10.3: `identity_allows_group` unconditional for
  restricted identities; the short-circuit skip keyed on `is_override_user_session`
  only. Pin test 19.
- **C4 — D6's registration instruction was a flag-day footgun**: `AUTH_BEARER_NAME_MAP`
  is read wholesale (`middleware/auth.py:19`), so a deployment declaring only the
  grouptoken entry silently un-maps `bearer`/`apikey` and every request degrades to
  anonymous 403s. **amended** — D6 and the docs now mandate showing the complete
  three-entry map.
- **C5 — two in-framework gates still honored the real user's global dict inside the
  token group**: `on_group_invite_member` (`rest/group.py:54`, `check_user=True`) and
  `GroupMember.can_change_permission` (`member.py:85`; same shape in
  `ApiKey.can_change_permission`, `api_key.py:204`) — a staff visitor's token could
  invite members / assign member perms in the gated group, which tenant-page JS could
  drive. **amended** — D10.7 applies the `is_override_user_session` discipline at all
  three sites; test 17.
- **C6 — test-plan gaps**: no Group LIST test, no endpoint-level chat tests, no
  docit/assistant tests, no `account=user-<other>` metrics test, no opt-in
  registration test (feasible via `th.server_settings`), no reference-mode ApiKey pin.
  **amended** — tests 2, 3, 14-19 added.

C-round areas that yielded **no substantive challenge** (attacked and held): the split
decision itself (no minting or JWT-upgrade path exists in this item's scope — handoff
and `auth/generate_api_key` both carry `denies_key_backed_session`; `refresh_token`
cannot parse a gt1 string); the `:555` elif restructure (all three fallthrough cases
traced — it is genuinely load-bearing: without it a global-`view_groups` token user
reaches the flat check and `Group.on_rest_handle_list` serves the entire Group table);
D8's method-sniffing (dispatch is strictly method-keyed; batch unreachable for User;
FK-attach arrives with the outer write verb and denies); the duck-type surface (every
`request.api_key` attribute read framework-wide is on the surface; the three
deliberately-unswapped sites — apikey whoami/rotate and the throttle resolver — are
correct as-is); signing/epoch/D6 mechanics fresh-verified.
